description: Every table that reaches academy_students through the foreign-key graph (directly or transitively), carries a student_id and NO tenant_id column, with the multi-tenant model each should follow. Issue #20 recorded these as 'need a tenant column'; reading the schema from pg_catalog showed that is the wrong default for almost all of them. Each keys uniquely on student_id (plus content dimensions such as locale or lesson), and every ON CONFLICT is on student_id, so by the current design one human is one learner across every tenant they are enrolled in. student-derived-table-classification.test.ts walks the full FK lineage and fails if such a table exists in the database but is absent here, or a classified table no longer exists or has since gained a tenant_id — so a new such table cannot ship unclassified (including one that reaches academy_students only indirectly) and a table that graduates to a tenant column cannot be left mis-described.

verdicts.student_global: Data about the learner, not about one tenant's programme: one row (or one row per content dimension) per human, shared across the tenants they belong to. There is no per-row tenant to leak. The isolation control is the binding check at the request edge — a route must resolve the acting tenant and confirm the session's student is bound to it (resolveTenantPrincipalContext) before serving the student's global data. No schema change; the remaining work is migrating the routes still on the legacy student-session path onto that resolver.
verdicts.tenant_partitioned: Data whose meaning is bounded by a tenant — activity inside one tenant's programme, or a row whose parent is already tenant-owned. The tenant is derived from that parent rather than invented, and the row gains the boundary plus a cross-tenant negative proof, joining tenant-scoped-table-registry.json once done.

notes.arena: The six academy_trading_arena_* tables look like per-tenant competition data, but academy_trading_arena_accounts.cycle_id is `UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` — a fresh id per account, not a shared competition period a tenant owns. So an arena run is per-student-session, not a tenant cohort, and partitioning it by tenant would be a product change (separate arenas per tenant for the same learner) rather than closing a leak. Classified student_global at the current design; revisit only if per-tenant arena competitions become a product requirement.
notes.reward_ledger: academy_reward_ledger (XP, badges) is the closest call. It is fed by global lesson completion (source_type 'official_section') and read only by student_id + locale today, so it is the learner's achievement record, not a tenant's economy. Classified student_global; a white-label customer wanting its own XP economy and leaderboard would move it to tenant_partitioned, which is a product decision, not a schema oversight.
notes.certificate_share_events: The one table with genuine tenant lineage: its certificate_id names a row in academy_certificates, which is already tenant-scoped and proven in tenant-scoped-table-registry.json. Its tenant is derived from that certificate rather than invented. Migration 0081 denormalises tenant_id/workspace_id onto the child and binds (certificate_id, tenant_id, workspace_id) to academy_certificates (id, tenant_id, workspace_id) as one composite FK — FK-binding certificate_id for the first time and making it structurally impossible for a share's tenant to diverge from its certificate's. Now tenant_partitioned and proven in tenant-scoped-table-registry.json.

tables.reason: The AI mentor's model of the learner. ON CONFLICT (student_id): one profile per human. A mentor profile does not become a different profile in a different tenant.
The learner's mentor chat history, keyed by student_id. The learner's relationship with the mentor is one relationship across tenants.
What the mentor remembers about the learner, keyed by student_id. Knowledge about the human, not about a tenant.
Derived insights about the learner, keyed by student_id. Global learner knowledge.
ON CONFLICT (student_id): the learner's one set of AI preferences, the same wherever they study.
The learner's practice attempts — learning history keyed by student_id, not a tenant's competition record.
Progress through lessons, unique on (student_id, locale, term_slug, section_key). A lesson is the same content in every tenant, so progress through it is the learner's, shared.
Assessment results per lesson, unique on (student_id, locale, lesson_id). The learner's learning record.
Term-level progress, unique on (student_id, locale, term_slug). The learner's record of a shared curriculum.
The learner's saved application state, unique on (student_id, locale). Belongs to the human, not a tenant.
Maps student_id to a pseudonymous public handle (public_student_id). Identity, one per human.
Frozen migration snapshots of the learner's progress, unique on (student_id, locale). Historical learner data.
Quarantined legacy rewards keyed to the learner's original_reward_id. Frozen learner history.
Badges the learner earned, unique on (student_id, achievement_id) and (student_id, code). Achievement history of the human.
Push tokens for the learner's devices, unique on (student_id, platform, token). A device belongs to the human; notifications route to the human.
Practice decisions in the simulator, unique on (student_id, scenario_id). Learning/practice history, keyed and read by student_id today.
A generic per-student event/telemetry log (event_type, payload, ip), keyed by student_id. Observability about the learner.

XP and badge ledger, unique on (student_id, locale, reward_key), fed by global lesson completion and read by student_id + locale. The learner's achievement record. See notes.reward_ledger for the product boundary that would move it.

A simulated trading account per student per cycle, but cycle_id defaults to a fresh gen_random_uuid() per account rather than a tenant-owned competition period. Per-student-session, not a tenant cohort. See notes.arena.

The attempts within an arena account, unique on (student_id, cycle_id, attempt_number) with a partial unique active-attempt index per student. It reaches academy_students only through academy_trading_arena_accounts, not by a direct foreign key, so it is a student-owned tenant-less table the direct-child walk originally missed (#430 review). Follows the per-student account. See notes.arena.
Idempotent arena commands hanging off an attempt; follows the account, which is per-student. See notes.arena.
Arena execution events per attempt/revision; follows the per-student account. See notes.arena.
Simulated trades in an arena attempt; follows the per-student account. See notes.arena.
Idempotent reflection commands, unique on (student_id, attempt_id, idempotency_key); follows the per-student account. See notes.arena.
Reflections on closed arena trades, unique on (student_id, attempt_id, closed_trade_id); follows the per-student account. See notes.arena.

Records a share of a certificate. Migration 0081 derives tenant_id/workspace_id from the parent academy_certificates and binds (certificate_id, tenant_id, workspace_id) to academy_certificates (id, tenant_id, workspace_id) as one composite FK, so certificate_id is FK-bound for the first time and a share's tenant can no longer diverge from its certificate's. Proven in tenant-scoped-table-registry.json. See notes.certificate_share_events.
